title: Efficient machine for randomized computation
statement: Let $M$ map pairs of bit strings to a bit, and suppose the verifier that returns $M(x,r)$ is efficient in the specified polynomial-time model. For any natural numbers $a,k$, there are natural numbers $K,e$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ such that, for every input $x$, on every choice word of length exactly $K(|x|^e+1)$ the machine halts; its output is a one-bit word; and for each bit $b$, the probability that its output is $b$ equals the probability that $M(x,u)=b$ when $u$ is uniformly chosen from bit strings of length $a(|x|+1)^k$. Moreover, on every such choice word, the output equals $M(x,u)$ for some bit string $u$ of that length.
